progress_notes.LISS-0426: complete 2026-08-13. || is always a single OR token at the lexer level (no context-sensitivity), so ||x|| is disambiguated from binary || purely by grammatical position (_primary vs _logical_or), matching how |x>/<x| already work. Found and fixed during Green: (1) the norm's own closing || was being swallowed by _logical_or as a binary operator while parsing its inner expression -- fixed with a _norm_bars_depth counter mirroring the existing _commutator_bracket_context precedent; (2) _infer_inner had no NormExpr case, silently falling through to Ty(State,Any) instead of Classical Float; (3) _bind had no standalone NormExpr case at all (only wired for the RHS of /), crashing on `Float n = ||a||` -- fixed by extracting a shared _compute_norm helper. Full regression 1532 passed; spec verification 100.00%.
progress_notes.LISS-0427: complete 2026-08-13. Reused OpBinder as a third kind alongside Sigma/Pi and LISS-0424's classical fold machinery, generalized to short-circuiting logical AND for ForAll. progress_notes.LISS-0430: complete 2026-08-13 -- largest Issue in the batch. Found a real, previously-dead pre-existing lexer bug: |x><x| (ADR 0169 Slice D) never actually worked anywhere, because _can_start_primary blocked < from starting a bra literal immediately after a closed ket -- confirmed zero existing corpus usage before fixing. Sigma over a named Set domain is resolved in _resolve_operator_tree (not the static lower_finite_binder_operators pass, which already fails gracefully there) by re-evaluating F's defining SetComprehension directly rather than threading the live Joint through the whole Operator-resolution chain. Verified at the matrix level (not just "doesn't crash") against hand-computed ground truth at n=2 and the full target n=3 shape, cross-checked against LISS-0429's own F={(1,0,1),(1,1,0)}. Full regression 1549 passed; spec verification 100.00%; full .sqx corpus staqex check clean.
progress_notes.LISS-0431: complete 2026-08-13. project's 'Renormalize after Lüders projection' block removed entirely, for every target shape, matching LISS-0422's own precedent (the equation writes projection and renormalization as two separate factors; project now does only the projection, LISS-0426's /||...|| does the renormalization).
